published_prior_art.cite: ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 fixes the bridge system and sample ratio; MareisDrton2026 optimizes a different linear front-door partial-measurement design.
GuptaLiptonChilders2024 and WangWangMiao2023 establish pilot/online efficiency-bound allocation for supplied fixed moment or influence-function systems, not subset-role bridge systems.

ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 gives fixed-system bridge inference and CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 uses independent pre-experimental selection; their combination is not a new frontier without a fully specified selected-design variance functional.
CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 studies cost-constrained residual variance divided by sample size, whereas the stated counterexample attacks uncosted raw prediction risk R_d(P).
none located: the checked long-term-proxy and collection-design papers do not give a primitive inverse-operator condition bounding this bridge-model prediction-to-efficiency ratio.

novelty_flags.label: thm:predictive-impossibility and related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The proposal calls its raw-risk selector the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm prediction criterion, but that paper minimizes residual variance divided by jointly chosen sample size subject to a cost constraint, not R_d(P) alone.

novelty_flags.label: thm:predictive-impossibility
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed refutation targets argmin R_d(P), yet no named published workflow in the core uses that uncosted selector; CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 instead uses sigma^2(gamma)/n under c(I(gamma),n)<=B, so the current negative kernel is hard-capped at letter, below novelty_target=field.

soundness_flags.label: thm:budget-profile
soundness_flags.one_line: With the displayed floor counts, the finite-B normalized bound is B{V_E,d/n_E,B+V_O,d/n_O,B}, not exactly mathcal V_d(alpha;P); state the asymptotic limit or retain the integer-rounding residual.

soundness_flags.label: thm:postselection-wald
soundness_flags.one_line: widehat s_B^2 is only described generically and is never defined from the selected design, allocation, and tilde V_g,d,B, so its asserted consistency is not a determinate statement.

soundness_flags.label: ass:external-validity
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited persistent-confounding paper's external-validity assumption is tailored to its designated middle short-term outcome block, whereas this condition imposes invariance of the entire potential catalogue Z(a); retag and justify this stronger all-role transport condition or restrict the design family.

soundness_flags.label: ass:outcome-bridge-existence
soundness_flags.one_line: Because T_d is assumed bijective between the declared L2 spaces and E[Y|S_2d,S_1d,A,X,G=O] is square-integrable, the displayed observed outcome-bridge equation already has a unique L2 solution.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:pilot-oracle-regret and thm:postselection-wald
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Uniform pilot score-variance consistency and the finite-family weak--strong bridge learner rates are assumed high-level inputs, not derived from a concrete learner or primitive smoothness class.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Pilot selection, allocation optimality, and Wald coverage are conditional on the stated finite-family rate and variance-estimation assumptions.

source_verification_receipts.version: The Econometrics Journal 23(1), published journal version
source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3.2, equations (3.3)--(3.6), especially pp. 9--10 / displayed equations (3.4)--(3.5)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper formulates covariate-and-sample-size selection as minimizing MSE and equivalently sigma^2(gamma)/n subject to c(I(gamma),n)<=B; the prediction formulation remains budget constrained and includes n.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3.1, Assumption 3 and its external-validity discussion, pp. 366--367; Section 5, Assumption 8, pp. 373--374
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper's external-validity condition is attached to its specified sequential outcome configuration and its rate condition is formulated for one fixed bridge system; it does not state all-catalogue potential-outcome invariance as the standard external-validity condition.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace R_d(P) by an explicit cost-aware prediction comparator matching Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm, or restrict the negative theorem to an equal-per-unit-cost subclass and state precisely why its prediction objective then coincides with the published workflow.

Define widehat s_B^2 explicitly from widehat d_m, widehat alpha_m, N_E,B, N_O,B, and the selected foldwise source-score second moments; restate Theorem 1 as an asymptotic profile with the floor remainder displayed.

Either restrict external validity to every admissible middle-role projection or retag full-catalogue invariance as a novel transportability condition with a concrete recruitment/measurement setting where it is credible; then supply one feasible bridge learner yielding the uniform rates.

recommended_next_step: Revise the flagship negative theorem to attack a genuinely published cost-aware predictive-selection workflow and repair the finite-budget and variance-estimator definitions before re-reviewing for the field-tier floor.
